en: The Inscription and Eulogy on the Propagation of the Great Qin’s Orthodox Teaching (Jingjiao) in China, Composed by the Monk Jingjing of the Great Qin Monastery, with Preface.

Preface to the Inscription and Eulogy on the Propagation of the Great Qin’s Orthodox Teaching in China: It is thus: The eternal, true stillness is prior even to the primordial; the profound, numinous void is subsequent to all things.
Yet it is wondrously existent;
it governs the profound and grasps the transformative power of creation,
excelling all sages as the Primordial Honored One.
It is only the One, the Three-in-One, the Wondrous Body Without Origin, the True Lord, the Arhat.
With ten characters, the four directions are fixed;
the primordial wind is stirred to produce the two qi.
The dark void was transformed and heaven and earth opened;
the sun and moon revolved and day and night were established.
The Artisan fashioned the myriad things and thus established the first human being.
He was specially granted the title of Lianghe to pacify and transform the seas.
The nature of the primordial source is empty and never overfilled;
the mind of original purity is fundamentally free from desire and craving.
Reaching even unto the false constructions of Sāṃkhya,
where the pure essence is adorned with ornaments;
within this, the distinctions between the great and the small are vast.
The interstices and obscurities are identical within that which is non-self;
thus, the three hundred and sixty-five types follow one another like a continuous trail of wheels.
They vied with one another in weaving the *dharmaparyāya*,
either pointing to specific objects to establish their tenets,
or sinking into the duality of emptiness and existence.
Some pray and sacrifice in pursuit of blessings;
others boast of their own excellence to deceive others;
their intellects and deliberations are restless and distracted.
Bound by the toil of worldly obligations,
one remains bewildered and gains nothing; oppressed and driven,
one is consumed by ever-increasing anguish.
Accumulated ignorance has long obscured the path, and delusion persists without restoration.
Thereupon, the Honored One Amitābha, a partial manifestation of my third body,
concealed his true majesty.
The people of Tongren came forth to serve as his successor.
Heaven and the gods proclaimed their joy;
a maiden gave birth to the Sage.
When auspicious signs were announced in the Jingxiu mansion during the reign of the Da Qin,
the Persians beheld its brilliance and presented offerings.
This contains the ancient teachings spoken by twenty-four holy ones.
In governing the principles of the state and the family through the Great Way,
he established the new teaching of the Three-in-One Pure Wind and the Wordless;
he refined excellent conduct through Right Faith.
He established the measure for the eight objects of perception,
refining the mundane dust into the Real;
he opened the gate of the Three Constants.
It opens the gates of birth, death, and extinction;
like the sun suspended in the sky, it shatters the dark treasury,
whereby the delusions of Māra are utterly crushed.
Rowing the boat of compassion to ascend to the Hall of Enlightenment,
all sentient beings have thus reached the further shore;
their task is hereby completed.
At noon, he ascended to the realm of the Real;
twenty-seven scriptures remained behind,
and Zhang Yuanhua opened the Gate of Spirit.
The wind of the Dharma-bath water washes away superficial splendor and purifies the empty whiteness;
it bears the seal of the ten characters.
Merging the four illuminations to harmonize with the unconditioned,
he strikes wood to vibrate the sound of benevolence and kindness;
toward the east, he pays homage and hastens upon the path of flourishing life.
One retains the beard to manifest external conduct;
one shaves the crown of the head to eliminate internal passions;
and one does not keep slaves or servants.
He equalized the noble and the humble among men;
he did not accumulate wealth, demonstrating that even his remaining possessions were left behind for me.
Through the fasting of the *zhai*, he subdued his consciousness and attained perfection.
The precepts are made firm through stillness and vigilance.
By performing prostrations and praises throughout the seven periods of the day,
one provides great protection for both the living and the deceased.
Offering once every seven days,
they cleanse their minds and return to simplicity;
this is the Way of True Permanence.
Sublime and difficult to name,
its efficacy is manifest;
it is tentatively termed the "Luminous Teaching" (Jingjiao).
Truly, the Way is not propagated without the Sage;
the Sage is not great without the Way.
The Way and the Sage are like a tally and its counterpart.
The world is civilized: Emperor Wenzong.
His glorious majesty inaugurates the era;
his brilliant sagacity presides over the people.
In the kingdom of Daqin (the Great Qin),
there was one of supreme virtue named A-lo-ben (Ānanda).
He perceived a green cloud and brought forth the True Sūtras.
Riding at the wind’s pace through hardships and perils, he arrived in Chang’an in the ninth year of the Zhenguan era.
The Emperor dispatched the Prime Minister, Lord Fang Xuanling, to lead the imperial guards to the western outskirts to welcome him into the palace.
He translated scriptures within the palace halls and inquired about the Way within the imperial precincts;
he possessed a profound understanding of the ultimate truth.
He was specially commanded to transmit [the teachings].
In the seventh month of the autumn of the twelfth year of the Zhenguan era, an imperial edict stated:
"The Way has no constant name."
The Sage has no fixed essence;
he establishes teachings according to circumstances to secretly deliver all living beings.
The Venerable Master Aluoben of the Great Qin Kingdom traveled from afar to bring scriptures and images to present to the capital;
having examined the principles of his teachings in detail:
Profound and wondrous, unconditioned—
contemplate its primal source and the essential principles for establishing existence.
The words are free from prolixity;
the principle lies beyond the trap.
Thus, it benefits all things and assists humanity.
"It is appropriate to propagate this throughout the world.
Thereupon, the authorities immediately established the Da Qin Monastery in Yining Ward of the capital and ordained twenty-one monks.
The virtue of the Zhou dynasty declined;
the Blue Carriage ascended to the West.
The Great Tang illuminates the Way.
As the auspicious winds fanned from the east,
the Emperor commanded the relevant officials to copy his true likeness onto the temple walls;
his celestial countenance overflowed with radiant colors.
The Yinglang and Jing gates shine with brilliance;
sacred traces radiate auspiciousness,
forever illuminating the Dharma-realm.
According to the *Xiyu tujiji* (Record of the Western Regions with Illustrations) and the historical annals of the Han and Wei dynasties,
the kingdom of Daqin (the Roman Empire) extends southward to the Sea of Coral and reaches northward to the Mountains of Many Treasures.
To the west it gazes upon the flower groves of the immortal realms;
to the east it borders the Long Wind Sea and the Weak Water.
From its soil emerge fire-washing cloth, soul-returning incense, bright-moon pearls, and night-shining jade.
The common people have no bandits or thieves;
the populace enjoys peace and well-being.
Yet, the Dharma cannot prevail without a model.
The sovereign does not establish himself without virtue;
thus his domain is vast and expansive,
and its culture and institutions flourish and shine.
The Great Emperor Gaozong was able to reverently continue the legacy of his ancestors and refine the True Doctrine.
Furthermore, Jing-temples were established in each of the provinces,
and Arahan was enshrined as the Great Dharma Master for the Pacification of the State;
thus the Dharma flowed throughout the Ten Circuits.
The state’s wealth is fundamentally at rest;
temples fill the hundred cities.
The households abound in auspicious blessings.
In the Shengli era,
the Buddhist monk Yongzhuang raised his voice in the Eastern Zhou region.
At the end of the Xiantian era,
the base scholars laughed aloud,
slandering [the teachings] in the western capital of Hao.
There were Sengshou, Lalitavajra, Huihan, Daode, and Jielie—noble lineages from the Western Regions and eminent monks beyond the mundane world.
Together they upheld the profound net of the Dharma and jointly restored the severed cords of the teachings. [This was during the reign of] Emperor Zhidao of the Xuanzong era.
He commanded the five kings, including Ningguo, to personally attend the auspicious halls to establish the ritual altars.
Thus, the pillars of the Dharma, though briefly bent, were raised once more;
the stones of the Path, though momentarily tilted, were set upright again.
At the beginning of the Tiānbǎo era,
the Great General Gāo Lìxī was ordered to escort [the portraits] to Wǔshèng Xiězhēn Temple for installation,
and one hundred rolls of silk were bestowed as a gift.
I respectfully celebrate the sagely destiny:
though the dragon whiskers are far removed,
the bow and sword may still be reached.
The sun’s corner radiates its light;
the Heavenly Countenance is but a few inches away.
For three years, there has been the monk Jiehe in the kingdom of Da Qin.
Gazing at the stars to seek transformation and looking toward the sun to pay homage to the Honored One,
he issued an edict for seventeen monks, including Sengluo, Hancheng, and Sengpu, among others.
Together with the Venerable Jiehe,
he performed meritorious deeds at Xingqing Palace; thereupon,
he inscribed the plaque for Tianyi Temple.
Upon his brow he wears dragon-script inscriptions,
adorned with jewels of shimmering azure that blaze like crimson dawn.
The wise decree expands the void;
soaring above and surging forth,
it proclaims that the bestowed favors are as lofty and steep as the Southern Mountains.
The沛澤 (Pàizé) marsh and the Eastern Sea are equally deep.
There is no Way that cannot be realized;
that which can be realized is what may be named.
The Sage’s deeds were all-encompassing,
and his achievements may be recounted: Emperor Wenming of the Sushong era established [the capital] across five commanderies, including Lingwu.
The Jing Temple was re-established;
with Yuan Shan providing support, blessings and prosperity flourished.
As great celebration arrived, the imperial enterprise was established—thus it was for Emperor Daizong Wenwu.
He expanded the sagely mandate and applied himself to the practice of non-action;
on each anniversary of his birth, he...
Incense from the celestial realm was offered to announce the successful completion of the rite;
imperial delicacies were distributed to illuminate the assembly.
Furthermore, because the Qian trigram embodies beautiful benefit, it is able to bring forth vast life.
The Sage, by embodying the fundamental source, is able to regulate and nourish all things. I, the Holy, Divine, Martial, and Cultured Emperor, who Establishes the Mean,
have examined the eight administrative measures to promote the worthy and demote the obscure,
and have expounded the nine categories of the Great Plan to renew the glorious mandate.
Transformation penetrates the profound principle;
the prayer is free from a sense of shame.
As for the vastness and emptiness of the universe:
Dedicated to stillness and practicing empathy,
he extensively bestows compassion to rescue the multitude from suffering,
and his skillful generosity covers all living beings.
This is the grand path for my practice and the gradual stages for my spiritual advancement.
If only the winds and rains would come in their proper seasons.
When the world is tranquil,
the person can bring order;
when things are pure, they can be clarified.
While alive, one can flourish;
after death, one can find joy.
A thought arises, and the resonance follows like an echo.
That "the emotions are aroused and the eyes are sincere" is the efficacy of my venerable power and the function of his service.
The Great Donor, Jinzi Guanglu Dafu...
He served concurrently as Deputy Commander of the Shuofang Military Command and was appointed Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Insignia.
He was granted a purple monastic robe, and his name was recorded as the monk Yisi.
Harmonious and fond of bestowing kindness,
he heard the Way and practiced it with diligence;
from afar, he came from the city of Rājagṛha.
Having come to the Central Lands,
his techniques surpassed those of the Three Dynasties;
his arts were as comprehensive as the Ten Perfections.
He first began to serve with disciplined propriety in the vermilion court,
and was subsequently enrolled among the ranks at the royal pavilion.
He was Gongsun Ziyi, the Grand Secretary and Prince of Fenyang.
When he first assumed supreme command in Shuofang, Suzong sent him along with his own retinue;
though treated with such intimacy as to be within the Emperor's private chambers,
he did not consider himself distinct from the ranks of common soldiers.
He served as the fangs and claws for the lord,
acting as the ears and eyes of the army,
and was able to distribute the emoluments and gifts.
He did not accumulate wealth within his own household;
he presented crystal bowls as tokens of his profound gratitude and spread golden carpets for his guests to rest upon.
Some maintained their existing monasteries,
while others expanded the Dharma halls and magnificently adorned the corridors and buildings.
Like a pheasant soaring in flight,
he further emulates the Gate of Radiance;
relying on benevolence, he bestows benefit.
Every year, the monastics from four temples assemble to perform devoted services and provide refined offerings throughout the entire fifty-day period.
Those who were hungry were fed;
those who were cold were clothed;
and those who were ill were treated and restored to health.
The deceased are buried and brought to rest.
As for the purity of one's integrity,
even Daśa has not heard of such excellence.
I, Baiyi Jingshi,
behold this person now and wish to carve a grand monument.
To extol his illustrious achievements, the inscription reads: "The True Lord has no origin;
he is profoundly still and eternally so."
He initiated the craftsmanship of transformation,
establishing the earth and setting up the heavens;
he manifested divided bodies to appear in successive ages.
Saving the boundless,
as the sun rises and darkness vanishes,
all realize the profound mystery. Glorious is the Emperor Wen!
His Way surpassed that of former kings;
he rode upon the times to dispel chaos.
Heaven was made vast and Earth was spread wide.
The luminous Jingjiao (Nestorianism) declares its return to our Tang;
let the scriptures be translated and monasteries be established.
A vessel for the living and the deceased;
may a hundred blessings arise together,
bringing peace to the myriad realms as the High Ancestor succeeds his forebears.
Furthermore, he constructed magnificent temples;
the imperial palace was spacious and bright,
filling the entire central land.
The True Way is clearly manifested;
accordingly, the Master of the Dharma is enfeoffed.
May all people enjoy peace and well-being.
All things are free from calamity and suffering; the August Emperor has revealed his sagehood.
He is able to cultivate the true and correct, and the imperial edict spreads its brilliant luster.
The celestial script shines in profusion;
the imperial domain dazzles with brilliance.
All lands within the four seas pay their highest reverence.
All administrative achievements flourished;
the people relied upon his blessings. When Emperor Suzong returned to the capital, the majesty of Heaven led his carriage.
The sacred sun spreads its brilliance;
auspicious winds sweep away the night.
Sovereign fortune returns to the Imperial House.
The demonic miasma is forever dispelled;
the boiling cauldron is stilled and the dust settled.
You have established our realm and summer; Your Majesty, Emperor Daizong, is filial and righteous.
His virtue accords with Heaven and Earth;
he opens up and bestows the process of generation and growth,
so that all things receive his beautiful benefits.
Incense is used to repay merit;
benevolence is practiced as an act of giving.
From the valley of the rising sun, your majesty arrives.
The essence of the Way is fully gathered in the Moon Cave; he establishes the ultimate standard of the Middle Kingdom.
He cultivates illustrious virtue and brings the four oceans into awe.
His literary brilliance illuminates the myriad realms;
his enlightened presence shines upon the hidden depths of humanity;
he observes the colors of all things as if looking into a mirror.
The six directions are bright and awakened;
the hundred tribes take it as their model.
How vast is the Way!
One should contemplate its profound strength.
The names and phrases unfold the triad of unity; the sovereign is able to act, while the minister is able to describe.
An imposing monument is erected to praise supreme auspiciousness.
The inscription was composed by the monk Wen of the Forest (Senwen).

One thousand one hundred and seventy-nine years after the monk Huichun reverently honored the True [Buddha], in the Jihwei year of the Xianfeng era (1859), Han Taihua of Wulin came to view [the stele]. Fortunate that the calligraphy remained intact, he reconstructed the stone pavilion to cover it. Alas, his late friend, the Provincial Governor Wu Zibi, was unable to join him on this excursion; for this reason, he felt deep regret for a long time.
